headphone-sony-zx310ap.review: Good, balanced, on-ear. The mic is OK for calls too. The K800's mic is better, but that's because it points straight at your mouth. A cheap and cheerful on-ear; Sony fanboys who want to collect Sony gear can start here.

headphone-snowsky-wind.review: Better to just take the Audio-Technica S120C: better tonality, safer tuning. Even the Sony ZX310AP is far better. This is very bright; it only wins on the Koss-style scene looks.

headphone-gaming-audeze-maxwell-wireless.review: God-tier, crazily well-packed features: 80-hour battery, AI mic, detachable mic, custom EQ in the phone and desktop apps, an adjustable mixer for sidetone (hearing your own voice + the game), and a lag-free USB-C dongle that plugs into PC, phone and PlayStation.

headphone-gaming-hyperx-cloud-3.review: A neutral tuning. The fit is super OK, comfortable for me. The mic is really good too. The wired version is a bit hard to drive louder, and its mic volume is a bit lower than the wireless one; otherwise more or less the same. The wired version has its own little sound card. A very, very neutral tuning: less sub-bass, a bit more treble, less upper mids (I'd prefer the upper mids raised a little). Better neutrality than the Inzone H3, and not as bright as the H3.

headphone-gaming-sony-inzone-h3.review: Sony's gaming line has the H3, H7 and H9, but for value for money just take the H3: much cheaper, no need for wireless, and the mic is far better than the wireless ones. Weakness: no ANC or Bluetooth, but for me that's not even a weakness. There's an app for custom EQ and gain, and it's DISCORD certified. Good mic.

headphone-gaming-sennheiser-gsp300-301-3.review: Only weird people doubt Sennheiser. Sony's gaming line is called INZONE; Sennheiser's is EPOS. The PC38X is really good, but I'm too lazy to buy it since it's pricey, so I suggest this. The earpads are replaceable. Comfortable, around the ear, light. Good mic too.

headphone-gaming-jbl-quantum-100.review: Good mic. Balanced-warm sound. The fit is OK. Plenty enough for a newbie, and light on the head. The GSP300 is slightly more neutral, but this doesn't end up bassy either, just balanced-warm. Lovely clarity, imaging and separation. I think it can really compete with wireless ones under a million, or even under 2 million.

headphone-gaming-audio-technica.review: Balanced to warm. The earpads aren't fully over-ear on me; they still press a little. But the sound is clearly better than buying a cheap TikTok wireless headphone. The cable obviously helps: clear. The mic is OK too.

headphone-gaming-edifier-k800.review: The Edifier K800 is something I bought on a whim, but it's good. Cheap and cheerful for people who do meetings, phone calls and Discord. The mic is really, really good, competing with the two above. And the sound is really lovely too; honestly like a headphone of 500k and up: balanced, not stinging. But not without weaknesses: a plastic case, no padding on the headband for your hair, and on-ear pads, so it's a bit less comfortable, but still very OK for people who just want a headphone to have.

headphone-gaming-sony-zx310ap.review: Good, balanced, on-ear. The mic is OK for calls too. The K800's mic is better, but that's because it points straight at your mouth. A cheap and cheerful on-ear; Sony fanboys who want to collect Sony gear can start here.

eartips-infitear-ie45-pro.review: Like the JVC Spiral Dot++, but not as flat/short, and the bore diameter isn't as wide as the JVC; it still has the dot pattern inside. What I hear: it keeps the sub-bass reasonably present rather than losing it like the JVC, and the top of the treble and the upper mids don't get shoutier. Very comfortable. Tested on the Xuan NV, Soratune Yi01 and Kinera Wyvern: all gained deep sub-bass, but not boosted. The treble is a touch warmer.

eartips-acoustune-aet08.tagline: Discontinued; if you find it, it may be a KBEAR copy
eartips-acoustune-aet08.review: The strangest eartip: it claims to widen the lower mids, and it really does; I think it also adds a little punch. It can make a bright IEM a little warmer. I mostly use this and the Azla Sedna EarFit Light when I need to adjust brightness; those two are my go-tos. AET08's weakness: sometimes it doesn't stay on well on IEMs whose nozzles have no lip, the straight, smooth ones.

eartips-softears-uc.review: Medical-grade silicone. It preserves clarity and keeps the soundstage from getting congested. Pleasant, and suits IEMs with big shells too. The material feels a bit tacky, like Xelastec, but nice. The tube isn't as short as Xelastec's, a bit longer, so the soundstage stays fairly well preserved, though not as wide as AET08 and with less bass than AET08. Fairly neutral and clear. Good for people who want more clarity while keeping the soundstage.

eartips-jvc-spiral-dot.review: Expensive, but really cool. Although it's a bit short, it keeps the clarity and the soundstage, maybe because of the dots. Keep in mind it's the DOTS++, not the regular Dots. It also works on TWS like the Sony WF-1000XM4 and fits in the case really well.

eartips-jvc-spiral-dot-stress-free.review: Available in ML and MS sizes if you need a more precise fit. Good upper midrange, slightly less treble. Very comfortable and light. The umbrella has a cut-away tail. Super comfortable and light; I thought the short umbrella would feel loose, but not at all. The space it gives is pleasant. "Less pressure on the ear", says the brand.

eartips-feaulle-h570.review: Wide and flat. It makes the upper mids clear, with less bass of course. An alternative to the Azla Sedna EarFit Short and Softears UC. Really suits the Tin HiFi C3.

eartips-spinfit-neo.review: Very comfortable in the ear. Comes with nozzle extensions for IEMs with short nozzles. The sound is WARM, that's it, but the bass doesn't get much bigger. More or less like Final Type E: the kind that warms the treble. Suits the C3 MK II.

eartips-spinfit-w1.review: Good clarity, good midrange. The shape is a bit stiffer, not as soft as the CP145. A wide bore, so the upper mids/treble come out bright and clear. But the tube is a bit long. I use it on the Chu 2, whose nozzle is fairly long: a good match, with the soundstage well preserved.

eartips-dunu-stage-studio.review: Adds upper mids/treble. The fit is very OK, surprisingly nice despite the super unique shape. The soundstage stays well preserved. I still prefer AET08 for soundstage.

eartips-azla-sedna-earfit-short.review: Works on the Soundcore Liberty 3 Pro and fits in the case. Insanely nice: excellent fit and resolution. Also suits the KZ ESX: great, thick midrange that opens up. Nice.

eartips-final-audio-type-e.review: Use this if you want your IEM to sound bassier. The treble doesn't attack, and the mids get a little less revealing, but it's so fun to use, I swear: pleasant and exciting. Also suits cheap IEMs like the TRN MT1 Max, Salnotes Zero and KZ DFi.

eartips-tangzu-sancai.review: Warms things up. I use it on the Sennheiser MTW3 and Liberty 3 Pro TWS and they fit the cases; there's a Sancai-specific EQ in the TWS section of the book. The material is like medical equipment in hospitals. A fairly wide bore that preserves the midrange well. It has a crumbly texture but is super comfortable on my MTW3. I haven't yet found an IEM it suits.

eartips-xelastec-sedna.review: Use this if you want to reduce bass and add treble. Annoyingly the soundstage shrinks a bit because the tip is a bit too short for my taste. But it's one of the ones with a really good fit, and it shortens the distance from tip to ear if you need that for an IEM with a too-long nozzle. The material is cool: the more you use it, the more it remembers the shape of your ear canal.

eartips-dekoni-mercury-foam.review: I use this for PLANARS only, to extremely tame a bright IEM or spicy treble. Keep in mind foam feels different and the seal gets very, very tight. Nice that it's washable, though foam doesn't last as long as silicone. But it's really nice on my Tin HiFi P1 and Shuoer S12.

eartips-monoprice.review: One of the champion most comfortable eartips; it feels like you're not wearing eartips at all, lol. Soft and light somehow. Enjoyable. It adds bass, but not too punchy or anything.

eartips-final-audio-fusion-g.review: Suits the XM5 because the material is similar, hybrid silicone and foam, but thinner and more elastic than Sony's stock XM5 tips. A bit more open with slightly less bass. Fits verrry nicely on the XM5 without sacrificing ANC performance.

eartips-ortofon.review: Also one of the lightest, with champion comfort. The bass may not be very punchy, a bit soft and boomy, but not a problem. Try it; it's really nice.

eartips-acoustune-aex07.review: Also an enjoyable eartip: it trims the very top of the treble a little, while the upper mids and mids become enjoyably transparent. Good for vocals, and it reduces sub-bass slightly. The fit is nicer than Acoustune AET08, and it sounds lovely too.

eartips-divinus-velvet.review: Smooth and warm. A nice fit. Still energetic even though it's a bit warm. The fit is slightly nicer than AET08.

eartips-final-audio-type-e-for-tws.review: Wow, this is crazy good for TWS: on the Edifier NeoBuds Pro and the WF-1000XM4 too. The bass gets punchy and the upper mids bright. The best TWS eartips in my view. I've also tried them on the ATH-CKS50TW: really enjoyable. Nice fit, nice sound.

eartips-azla-sedna-earfit-light.review: One of the wide-bore eartips, which means it brightens the upper mids/treble a little. Usually the soundstage shrinks a bit, but since its tube is fairly long it doesn't shrink as much as Xelastec. Nice, enjoyable fit. I mostly use it on the Tin HiFi T3+, so the bass isn't too much. Nice on a single DD you feel has too much bass. One person complained it made their ears itch, but not me.

eartips-acoustune-aex70.review: Good soundstage, focused on treble clarity. The material is a bit thin. The fit is decent but lacks grip; if you want a lot of grip, try Dunu S&S, or Softears UC if you want a "full" feeling in the ear.

eartips-dunu-candy.review: Adds a little treble extension at the top, not in the upper midrange. Well-controlled bass. Its only weakness: a bit hard to put on.

eartips-pentacon-coreir.review: Don't. A waste: overpriced for eartips. It brightens things. Only suits short nozzles; when it fits, it fits really well and can make things better or warmer, like on my Letshuoer EJ07M. On long nozzles it catches on its brass part. I gave it a C for value because it's such a waste: very expensive. Just a shame.

eartips-spinfit-cp145.review: This is just safe, kind of neutral; I don't feel anything. It does the job well as an eartip, but has no particular character. Its headline feature is supposedly that it rotates comfortably to adjust the IEM's position.

eartips-tri-clarion.review: A standard wide bore. Brightens things. But it's cheap.

eartips-acoustune-aex50.review: Works on the Soundcore Dot 3i. It has wings, adding a little soundstage and midrange clarity. The wings feel a bit odd at first, but it fits in the case. If you need tips for a Dot 3i, go for it.

eartips-dekoni-bulletz-for-tws-foam.review: Great for TWS if you want a smooth, less aggressive sound. I use it on the Sony WF-1000XM4, not because its highs are harsh, but because it's just really nice and smooth.
